thesis: D. M. Sheen, 'Numerical modeling of microstrip circuits and antennas', PhD thesis, MIT, 1991 (PDF 238 pages; printed page number = PDF page index in this scan, verified on pp.7, 73, 108, 112, 159, 162, 163, 233)

low_pass_filter.source: Sec. 3.4 'Low Pass Filter', thesis pp.108-116 (PDF pp.108-116); page images pages/p108..p116_pdf*_render_w5088.png
low_pass_filter.design_reference: designed per criteria of ref.[25] D'Inzeo, Giannini, Sorrentino, 'Novel microwave integrated low-pass filters', Electronics Letters 15(9) 258-260, Apr. 1979 (p.108 text; bibliography p.233)
low_pass_filter.layout: two collinear-offset feed lines (ports 1 and 2, along y) attached to opposite long sides of a long rectangular patch (along x); each port line is set back 5.65 mm from the nearer patch end (Fig. 3.25)

substrate.loss_note: not stated; FD-TD excludes dielectric and conductor loss (p.136 text)

conductor.model: perfect conductor, tangential E set to zero on strips (p.76 Sec.3.1.2); thickness not given (zero-thickness sheet in FD-TD)

dimensions_mm_drawing.patch_length_src: Fig. 3.25 p.108 ('20.32 mm', arrow parallel to the patch, x)
dimensions_mm_drawing.TL_model_check: stub + spacing + stub = 6.857 + 6.607 + 6.857 = 20.321 mm = patch length 20.32 (Fig. 3.26 p.109)
dimensions_mm_drawing.port_line_length: not stated (Fig. 3.25 draws lines to the board edge; board size not dimensioned)

planar_model_p109.note: effective (fringing-extended) planar-circuit dimensions, eqs.(A.3),(A.5),(A.6); p2-p1 = 6.607 mm = port spacing

fdtd_model_p112.arith_sub: 0.794/0.265 = 2.996 -> 3 cells = 0.795 mm (thickness not stated in cells for this circuit; corner p.94 uses 3 dz)
fdtd_model_p112.arith_off: 5.65/0.3948 = 14.31 cells (thesis: port locations/widths modelled 'with some slight error smaller than the step size', p.109/112)
fdtd_model_p112.boundaries: first-order Mur-type ABC (2.51) on sides; top first- or second-order (2.62) (p.76; not stated which for this circuit)
INCONSISTENCIES: 50*dx = 19.74 mm but Fig. 3.25 gives 20.32 mm (would need dx = 20.32/50 = 0.4064 mm); p.109 says dx, dy were chosen to match the patch exactly
45 cells in y cannot hold 4 (source) + 30 (source->patch) + 6 (patch) + 10 (patch->port-2 reference plane) = 50 cells

p.109/p.112 also say the port locations and widths carry an error smaller than one step, which is consistent with 6 dx = 2.369 mm for the 2.413 mm lines, but not with 50 dx = 19.74 mm for the 20.32 mm patch

measurement.who: circuits and measurements provided by Mohamed Abouzahra (Acknowledgements p.5)
measurement.instrument: a network analyzer, model not stated; analyzer and connectors rated only to 18 GHz (p.136)
measurement.connectors: microstrip-to-coaxial transitions, type not stated; NOT compensated (no de-embedding) in the measurement (p.136)
measurement.calibration: not stated (beyond the transitions being uncompensated)
measurement.reference_planes: not stated for the measurement; FD-TD reference planes 10 dy = 4.232 mm from the patch edges (p.112)
measurement.frequency_range: measured dash-dot |S21| starts at 1.98-1.99 GHz and |S11| at about 1.98 GHz (Figs. 3.33/3.34); plotted to 20 GHz; data above 18 GHz are beyond the analyzer/connector rating (p.136)

line_fed_patch.source: Sec. 4.3 'Line Fed Rectangular Patch Antenna', thesis pp.158-163 (PDF pp.158-163)
line_fed_patch.conductor: perfectly conducting, tangential E = 0 (p.144 Sec.4.1.2); thickness not stated

dimensions_mm.src_feed: text p.158 ('nominally 50 ohm', 'width of 4.48 mm'), Fig. 4.11
dimensions_mm.feed_position: centre of one edge (p.158); Fig. 4.11: 20.1 mm from the patch corner to the feed centreline (20.1 = 40.2/2)

fdtd_model_p158_159.variable_grid: 3:1 variable gridding in x and y only: p.158 says spacings three times larger are used around the antenna, and p.159 says the 3-to-1 variable gridding is in the x and y directions (visible in Fig. 4.12). Outer cells 3*1.11667 = 3.35 mm in x/y; nothing in the text supports a 3x (1.59 mm) z cell.
fdtd_model_p158_159.Zin_reference: input impedance referenced to the front (feed) edge of the patch (pp.159-160)
fdtd_model_p158_159.boundaries: first-order ABC on the 4 side walls, second-order ABC on top, PEC ground (p.144)
fdtd_model_p158_159.n_steps_note: p.159: the run stops when the reference-plane response has decayed to about zero, or at 6000 dt (6000 is a cap, not a fixed length)

measurement.who: Deshpande and Bailey, ref.[22] 'Input impedance of microstrip antennas', IEEE Trans. AP-30(4) 645-650, July 1982 (bibliography p.233); Fig. 4.15 legend 'Measured by Deshpande and Bailey 82'
measurement.reference_plane: plotted relative to the patch front edge together with the FD-TD (Fig. 4.14); Fig. 4.15 Smith chart: same values (cross-check: R, X from Fig. 4.15 with Z0 = 50 ohm agree with Fig. 4.14 markers within a few ohm)
measurement.what_is_plotted: Zin = R + jX (ohm) at 7 frequencies (markers); no |S11| in dB is plotted; Smith chart Fig. 4.15 (normalisation not printed; consistent with 50 ohm)
measurement.thesis_statements: fundamental resonance approximately 2.275 GHz (p.158); FD-TD shows a small frequency shift of about 0.4 % (p.160)

figures.Fig. 4.14: Zin R,X: FD-TD (solid R, dashed X) and measured (* R, o X), p.162
figures.Fig. 4.15: Smith chart: x FD-TD, o measured (Deshpande & Bailey), * MoM (Deshpande & Bailey), p.163

INCONSISTENCIES: p.117 says dx and dy are chosen to match the 9.75 mm centre-to-centre distance exactly, but the stated centre-to-centre distance 24*dx = 24*0.390 = 9.36 mm; 9.75 mm would need 25 cells of 0.390 mm or dx = 9.75/24 = 0.40625 mm
p.117 says dz matches the substrate exactly: 3*0.265 = 0.795 mm vs 0.794 mm (Fig. 3.35), i.e. exact to 0.001 mm

branch_line_coupler.measured_figures: Fig. 3.38 p.120 |S11|,|S21|,|S31|,|S41| FD-TD solid vs Meas dash-dot 0-10 GHz; Fig. 3.39 p.121 phase difference S31-S41 (not digitised)
